clue.text: Entomic specimens of Coolidge? (Repeatedly eponymous)

definitions.text: Entomic specimens
definitions.meaning: insect specimens: North American bush crickets named for their call

definitions.text: of Coolidge? (Repeatedly eponymous)
definitions.meaning: Susan Coolidge's heroine gives her name, repeatedly, to the titles What Katy Did, What Katy Did at School and What Katy Did Next

explanation.surface: A naturalist asks whether some insects belong to a writer named Coolidge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coolidge' looks like the US president; it is Susan Coolidge, author of the What Katy Did books, so the insects' name recurs in her titles.
explanation.definitionFit: The insects are named from their chirp, which sounds like 'Katy did', also the phrase in Coolidge's book titles.

clue.text: The Captain could be in hot water? On the contrary

definitions.text: The Captain could be in hot water? On the contrary

parts.words: The Captain could be in hot water? On the contrary
parts.note: Reversing the idea, hot water could be in the vessel that shares his surname

explanation.surface: A ship's captain finds himself in trouble, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kettle was a popular fictional sea captain; 'on the contrary' flips the sentence, so the hot water is inside the boiling vessel rather than the captain in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for boiling water, and also the surname of Cutcliffe Hyne's fictional sea captain.

clue.text: Hawk left one of these in Lewis

definitions.text: Hawk left one of these in Lewis

parts.words: Hawk left one of these in Lewis
parts.note: Sinclair Lewis's early novel is The Trail of the Hawk, so the hawk leaves a track in Lewis's book

explanation.surface: A bird of prey leaves tracks across the Hebridean island of Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis looks like the Scottish island; it is the novelist Sinclair Lewis, whose 1915 novel is The Trail of the Hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths or tracks left behind by something moving, as in the title of Lewis's novel.

clue.text: Your old place in terrible dim bar calls for a boisterous song

definitions.text: a boisterous song

indicators.note: the old pronoun is placed inside the rearranged letters of the bar
a terrible bar is one in bad shape, signalling that the letters of dim bar are jumbled

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A rowdy drinking song is called for in a dingy, awful pub that was once yours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your old place' reads as a former home, but it is the archaic possessive; 'terrible' scrambles the bar and 'in' sets the pronoun inside. A dithyramb was a Dionysian choral hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dithyramb was originally a wild choral hymn to Dionysus, hence any frenzied, impassioned song or poem.

clue.text: In which Dickens's tragic father finds consolation in Florence

definitions.text: In which Dickens's tragic father finds consolation in Florence

parts.words: In which Dickens's tragic father finds consolation in Florence
parts.note: in this Dickens novel the proud merchant, ruined and bereaved, is finally comforted by his neglected daughter Florence

explanation.surface: A grieving father from Dickens seeks solace on a trip to the Italian city of Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence is not the Italian city but Dombey's daughter, whom he neglects in favour of his son Paul until she comforts him at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Dickens novel whose merchant hero loses his son and fortune and is redeemed by his daughter's love.

clue.text: Shirley Hazzard's should perhaps not cast the first stone. Or indeed, any other

definitions.text: Shirley Hazzard's should perhaps not cast the first stone. Or indeed, any other

parts.words: Shirley Hazzard's should perhaps not cast the first stone. Or indeed, any other
parts.note: Hazzard's book is titled after the proverb about those in glass houses who should not throw stones; it also echoes 'let him without sin cast the first stone'

explanation.surface: A moralist suggests a novelist's characters should refrain from judging others.
explanation.walkthrough: Shirley Hazzard's story collection is People in Glass Houses, after the proverb that those who live in glass houses should not throw stones, first or otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: The first word of Hazzard's title and of the proverb: human beings in general.

clue.text: Given name of one who wrote of the fear of being

definitions.text: Given name of one who wrote of the fear of being

parts.words: Given name of one who wrote of the fear of being
parts.note: the first name of the ... novelist Jong, author of Fear of Flying and later Fear of Fifty

explanation.surface: A philosopher's first name is sought, the one who wrote on existential dread.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fear of being' sounds existential, but it points to Erica Jong's book titles beginning Fear of.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the novelist Jong, who wrote Fear of Flying.

clue.text: Undistinguished opera composer often successfully defended his king

definitions.text: Undistinguished opera composer often successfully defended his king

parts.words: Undistinguished opera composer often successfully defended his king
parts.note: the eighteenth-century French composer of comic operas was better known as the leading chess player of his day, with a defence named after him

explanation.surface: A minor opera composer is praised as a loyal royalist who saved his monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is a chess piece: the composer was the finest chess player of his age, and a chess opening, a defence, bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: François-André Danican, a modest composer of opéras comiques and a chess master famed for his defence.

clue.text: Vaughan saw it the other night

definitions.text: Vaughan saw it the other night

parts.words: Vaughan saw it the other night
parts.note: Henry Vaughan's poem The World opens 'I saw ... the other night, / Like a great ring of pure and endless light'

explanation.surface: Someone named Vaughan glimpsed something a few evenings ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Vaughan is a seventeenth-century Welsh metaphysical poet; the clue quotes the first line of his poem The World.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless time, the vision in the opening line of Vaughan's poem.

clue.text: Apostrophe to fall of one "whose name was writ in water "

definitions.text: Apostrophe to fall of one "whose name was writ in water "

parts.words: Apostrophe to fall of one "whose name was writ in water "
parts.note: Keats asked for the epitaph 'Here lies one whose name was writ in water'; his ode addressing the season of mists is an apostrophe, a direct address

explanation.surface: A grammar point about an apostrophe sits beside a line about a forgotten name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apostrophe' is not the punctuation mark but a poem addressed to someone or something; 'fall' is the American word for the season, and Keats's epitaph identifies the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Keats's ode addressed directly to the season after summer.

clue.text: A poet gets guidance from St Bernard in such a comedy

definitions.text: A poet gets guidance from St Bernard in such a comedy

parts.words: A poet gets guidance from St Bernard in such a comedy
parts.note: in the last cantos of Dante's Paradiso, Bernard of Clairvaux replaces Beatrice as Dante's guide

explanation.surface: A poet is led along by a St Bernard dog in a comic play.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Bernard suggests a rescue dog, but it is the saint who guides Dante at the end of Paradiso, the last part of his great poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective Dante's Commedia acquired in its title, meaning heavenly or godly.

clue.text: Butler did it — producing such lines

definitions.text: Butler did it — producing such lines

parts.words: Butler did it — producing such lines
parts.note: Samuel Butler's mock-heroic poem Hudibras gave its name to its jogging comic octosyllabic couplets

explanation.surface: A detective-story cliché: the butler did it, and the clue asks what lines he spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The butler did it' is the murder-mystery cliché, but Butler is Samuel Butler, the seventeenth-century satirist whose verse style is named after his poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel comic verse in the manner of Butler's Hudibras.

clue.text: Composer has quiet pause beginning yesterday

definitions.text: Composer

parts.note: a lull is a quiet pause or interval of calm

indicators.note: the beginning of yesterday is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A composer takes a short rest that started yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Baptiste Lully was the Italian-born composer at the court of Louis XIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lully, the Baroque composer of French opera.

clue.text: A dams wrote his own

definitions.text: A dams wrote his own

parts.note: Henry Adams wrote an autobiography in the third person titled The ... of Henry Adams

explanation.surface: A builder of dams writes his own memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A dams' is the American historian Henry Adams split as printed; his famous autobiography is called The Education of Henry Adams.
explanation.definitionFit: The schooling and learning described in the title of Henry Adams's autobiography.

clue.text: Book by Christopher Fry for sacred representation

definitions.text: Book by Christopher Fry for sacred representation

parts.words: Book by Christopher Fry for sacred representation
parts.note: Fry wrote the libretto (the 'book') for Penderecki's opera after Milton, which Penderecki called a sacra rappresentazione

explanation.surface: A playwright publishes a book for a religious pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' means the libretto of a stage work: Christopher Fry wrote the text for Penderecki's 1978 Milton opera, styled a sacred representation.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic of the Fall, which Fry adapted as Penderecki's libretto.

clue.text: "Ye elements! — in whose —— stir I find myself exalted" (Byron, Childe Harold)

definitions.text: "Ye elements! — in whose —— stir I find myself exalted" (Byron, Childe Harold)

parts.words: "Ye elements! — in whose —— stir I find myself exalted" (Byron, Childe Harold)
parts.note: the missing word from Canto IV of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage, describing the elements' uplifting motion

explanation.surface: A quotation from Byron with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the gap from Byron's Childe Harold's Pilgrimage: the elements' stir raises the poet up, matching 'exalted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising in dignity or rank, which suits the speaker finding himself exalted.

clue.text: Condition in which Bates got his goat

definitions.text: Condition in which Bates got his goat

parts.words: Condition in which Bates got his goat
parts.note: a story in which a character called Bates gains his goat while flying in the air

explanation.surface: Somebody called Bates becomes irritated by some situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got his goat' looks like the idiom for being annoyed, but read literally it describes acquiring an animal while flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried through the air, the state in which the goat was got.

clue.text: Churchill associated them with adventures

definitions.text: Churchill associated them with adventures

parts.note: Winston Churchill's 1932 essay collection is titled ... and Adventures

explanation.surface: Churchill linked something with his escapades.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill's collection of essays is Thoughts and Adventures, so the missing word pairs with adventures in that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas or reflections, the word paired with adventures in Churchill's title.

clue.text: Character from Washington rather tousled on archaic bed

definitions.text: Character from Washington

indicators.note: tousled hair is dishevelled, so the letters of on and archaic bed are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from the US capital lies rumpled on an old-fashioned bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington is Washington Irving, not the city: his schoolmaster in The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. 'tousled' rearranges ON plus ARCHAICBED.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanky schoolmaster chased by the Headless Horseman in Washington Irving's tale.

clue.text: Rue tag designed for African language ..

definitions.text: African language

indicators.note: something designed is put together in a new form, so the letters of rue tag are rearranged

explanation.surface: A label for regret is created for a language from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges RUETAG. The Tuareg are Berber-speaking nomads of the Sahara, and the name is used for their language, Tamasheq.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Berber nomads of the Sahara, also called Tamasheq.

clue.text: … descriptive of finish overheard

definitions.text: … descriptive of finish overheard

parts.note: the word 'finish' heard aloud sounds like the language of Finland, which this word describes

explanation.surface: Someone describes an ending they eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 19, another language. 'finish overheard' sounds like 'Finnish', and the answer describes the Finns and their Scandinavian neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Of northern Europe and Scandinavia, an adjective covering Finland.

clue.text: Nobel prizewinner. A sort of gentleman on stage, Poquelin suggested

definitions.text: Nobel prizewinner
definitions.meaning: Léon ..., French statesman, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1920

definitions.text: A sort of gentleman on stage, Poquelin suggested
definitions.meaning: Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, better known as Molière, wrote Le ... gentilhomme, the middle-class would-be gentleman

explanation.surface: A Nobel laureate, and a play's would-be gentleman as an actor named Poquelin proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Poquelin was Molière's real surname; his comedy is Le Bourgeois gentilhomme. Léon Bourgeois won the 1920 Nobel Peace Prize for work on the League of Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Léon Bourgeois was a Nobel Peace laureate; the word also means middle-class, Molière's pretentious social climber.

clue.text: He had father and son in common with James T. Farrell

definitions.text: He had father and son in common with James T. Farrell

parts.words: He had father and son in common with James T. Farrell
parts.note: both Edmund ... and the American novelist Farrell published books titled Father and Son

explanation.surface: Two men share a father and a son with an American novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father and son' look like relatives but are a book title: Edmund Gosse's 1907 memoir and Farrell's 1940 novel share it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse, critic, whose memoir of his Plymouth Brethren father is Father and Son.

clue.text: Murdoch protagonist probably asleep?

definitions.text: Murdoch protagonist probably asleep?

parts.note: Iris Murdoch's novel ... Dream is named for its bedridden old hero, who is dreaming and so probably asleep

explanation.surface: A media magnate's main character is likely napping.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch suggests the media owner, but it is Iris Murdoch; her novel is Bruno's Dream, and a dreamer is probably asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The dying old man whose dream gives Murdoch's novel its title.

clue.text: New version of work concerning number sign

definitions.text: New version of work

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning concerning or about
a hash is the # symbol, also called the number sign

explanation.surface: A revised edition of a work deals with the number symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A reworking of old material presented again with little real change.

clue.text: Miss Holtby is said to be healing well

definitions.text: Miss Holtby is said to be healing well

parts.words: Miss Holtby is said to be healing well
parts.note: the Yorkshire novelist Holtby's first name is that of the Welsh saint whose well at Holywell is famed for cures

explanation.surface: A Miss Holtby is reported to be recovering nicely from illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Healing well' looks like recovery but is a holy spring: St Winefride's Well at Holywell in Wales is a place of pilgrimage. Holtby wrote South Riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Holtby's forename, shared with the Welsh saint whose spring is reputed to cure.

clue.text: A season of Yeats

definitions.text: A season of Yeats

parts.note: Yeats's poem on the Dublin Rising is titled after the spring festival during which it occurred, followed by the year 1916

explanation.surface: A series of Yeats plays or readings.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeats wrote 'Easter, 1916' about the Irish rising; 'season' means a church festival period, not a run of performances.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring Christian festival named in the title of Yeats's poem about the 1916 Rising.

clue.text: Describing the introduction, is eager and in charge

definitions.text: Describing the introduction

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: Someone introducing an event is keen and running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for introductory study, especially of a subject's foundations.
